title: The performance and psychological effects of goal setting in sport: a systematic review and meta-analysis
publisher: International Review of Sport and Exercise Psychology
claims: Goal setting improved task performance in sport, with effects differing by goal type: process goals d = 1.36, performance goals d = 0.44 and outcome goals d = 0.09.

The review reports a non-significant performance difference between specific (d = 0.37) and non-specific goals (d = 0.72), and effects differing by goal type; the abstract does not report moderation by proximity, experience or feedback.
The review reports mixed performance findings and limited cross-study evidence for some psychological outcomes.
